correctness.rationale: Every map is uniquely an interval kernel partition and increasing image subset. Mutual inverses are exactly reciprocal transversals, giving A(X)=M X^T M. The rows of M are independent over every field by induction on the last variable of the squarefree partition polynomials. Its real singular-value decomposition yields a(a+1)/2 positive, a(a-1)/2 negative and a(b-a) zero eigenvalues at rank r; Vandermonde identities yield the global central-binomial rank and inertia. An independent direct enumeration of all maps and inverse conditions up to n=5 agrees with the incidence factorization and full-rank lemma, and a numerical eigensign check agrees through n=5. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact rank-stratum and global real inertia statements were compared by implication with the full accessible 2024 inverse-matching paper, relevant 2019 and 2015 material, the abstract and metadata of the October 2026 primary work, indexed research records, and accessible prior results on inverse-degree statistics. Matching existence and scalar inverse-degree moments do not determine adjacency-matrix rank or inertia. The full 2026 primary text remains inaccessible, so this is a qualified originality determination, not a global priority certification.

value.rationale: The inverse-pair relation is the graph-theoretic object behind the current monoid matching problem. Its exact real rank and positive/negative inertia are natural global structural invariants that neither matching existence nor scalar inverse-degree formulas determine. The theorem covers every chain size and every image-rank block, with a simple closed central-binomial global rank and a constructive mechanism through interval-transversal incidence. It is a nontrivial all-parameter classification of the signature, not a small finite census, a parameter substitution, or a claim about unproved future matching consequences.
